findings.passage: One unnamed friend said: "Frankly, the real Tiger Woods isn't that marketable. There isn't a lot of money to be made off a guy who just wants to be left alone to read a book." Another: "Tiger was a natural introvert, and the financial interest for him to be extroverted really drove a wedge in his personality."
findings.problem: Speaker error that invents a second corroborating witness. In the full text of Thompson's April 21, 2016 ESPN feature (S17), both lines are one continuous quotation from a single unnamed friend: '"Frankly, the real Tiger Woods isn't that marketable," a friend says. "There isn't a lot of money to be made off a guy who just wants to be left alone to read a book. Or left alone to play fetch with his dog. ... Do you see a trend? Tiger was a natural introvert, and the financial interest for him to be extroverted really drove a wedge in his personality."' The draft splits it into 'One unnamed friend ... Another', FAQ 3 repeats the split in a search-visible answer ('One friend told ESPN's Wright Thompson that Woods was "a natural introvert," another that he "just wants to be left alone to read a book"'), and the Uchitel paragraph says 'what unnamed friends told one reporter'. The Five case and the man-versus-persona thread both lean on this testimony, so overstating its independence matters. The evidence record (C12, C91, C93) has the same error.
findings.acceptance_test: The body attributes both lines to the same unnamed friend (for example, 'One unnamed friend said: "...read a book." The same friend added: "Tiger was a natural introvert..."'), with any omission marked by an ellipsis. FAQ 3 attributes both phrases to one friend. 'what unnamed friends told one reporter' becomes singular. C12, C91 and C93 are corrected to one speaker. No sentence in the body, FAQs or evidence implies two independent friends.

findings.passage: Jordan was speaking six years after the apology. A man who wants the record erased is still living inside other people's picture of him.
findings.problem: Context error in the stated discriminator. In S17, between Thompson's 'He hears everything.' and Jordan's 'That bothers him more than anything,' Thompson writes: 'For Tiger, this dwelling on old mistakes is a path to madness. Nothing can take him back to 2006 and give him a second chance.' Jordan then says: 'It looms. It's in his mind. It's a ship he can't right and he's never going to. What can you do? The thing is about T-Dub, he cannot erase. That's what he really wants. He wants to erase the things that happened.' The draft's splice drops the bridge, so 'That' seems to point at public commentary, while in the source it follows regret over old mistakes and a lost second chance. The draft builds on that reading three times: 'A man who wants the record erased' turns 'erase the things that happened' (the events) into the public record; the One rebuttal says 'Jordan describes torment over what people say', although regret over the acts is what the draft says a One's inner critic produces; and the Five rebuttal says Jordan 'worries about a man who can't stop reading it', where Thompson wrote 'perhaps sitting up in the middle of the night reading'. The evidence record's own alternatives for C95 and C132 note this limit; the prose does not. Since this passage carries the Three over the Eight, Five and One, the overreach goes to the core of the type argument.
findings.acceptance_test: (1) The Jordan passage conveys Thompson's bridging framing, quoted or accurately summarized ('dwelling on old mistakes', no 'second chance'), so 'That bothers him' keeps its source referent. (2) 'wants the record erased' is replaced with wording faithful to 'He wants to erase the things that happened'. (3) The One rebuttal ('What tips against the One...') no longer says Jordan describes torment only over what people say. It rests the image reading on the reading-what-people-write and 'Rabbit Ears' details, labeled as Thompson's report of Jordan's worry, and concedes that wanting to undo the past fits a One's inner critic or ordinary regret as well. (4) 'can't stop reading it' matches Thompson's 'perhaps ... reading'. (5) C81, C95, C130, C132 and C133 are updated to match. Confidence stays medium or is reconsidered explicitly, and the repaired paragraph is reverified.

findings.passage: Nothing shows Woods made the 2007 deal.
findings.problem: Slight understatement against the article's own cited source. HuffPost (S10) relays the Wall Street Journal, citing 'people directly involved in the arrangement', that 'Mr. Woods agreed to the cover shot and photo spread in Men's Fitness ... in return for the National Enquirer squelching a story', and that when approached, Woods' reps 'almost immediately "made an offer"'. So 'Nothing shows' and the protected 'There is no public record of what Woods himself said or decided' go further than the record. What is missing is a first-hand or on-record account of his personal role, not any reporting at all. The error leans toward the subject and leaves the argument unaffected (the crisis sequence is correctly treated as non-discriminating), but it is a factual characterization of a cited source.
findings.acceptance_test: The type section and/or the 2007 paragraph say accurately that 2010 reporting (WSJ, citing people involved, via S10) said Woods agreed to the shoot in exchange for the story being dropped and that his representatives made the offer, while there is no first-hand account of his own role. The protected passage's separation of record from inference is kept. The conclusion that the crisis cannot separate a Three from an Eight may stand.

findings.passage: read a prepared statement about his affairs to an invited room at TPC Sawgrass in Florida. He took no questions.
findings.problem: Unsourced metadata-level fact. The venue and the no-questions format are true: AP (via MPR News, February 19, 2010) reports he spoke 'from the clubhouse at the TPC Sawgrass, home of the PGA Tour' and 'no questions were allowed'. But neither linked transcript (S02 inline, S01) says so, and no opened source in the inventory does, while C126 (FAQ 4: 'took no questions') cites only the transcripts. The 'unequal evidence' argument leans on the setting.
findings.acceptance_test: An opened source stating the venue and that no questions were taken (for example https://www.mprnews.org/story/2010/02/19/tiger-woods-speech) is added to the evidence with locator and excerpt. It is cited in C126 and linked at the hook or FAQ 4.

findings.passage: After a February 23, 2021, crash near Rancho Palos Verdes, California
findings.problem: Location does not match the cited source. The linked ESPN report (S41, April 7, 2021) places the crash 'in Rolling Hills Estates, just outside Los Angeles'. The site is on the Rolling Hills Estates / Rancho Palos Verdes border, so the draft is not false, but the passage's own citation does not support it.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence matches the cited source ('in Rolling Hills Estates, near Los Angeles') or cites an opened source for 'near Rancho Palos Verdes'. C32 is updated.

evidence.reason: Exceptional breadth and fidelity overall. I reopened 54 used sources, and nearly every quotation is verbatim with the right speaker, date and locator: the CNN and Globe transcripts, ASAP 2022, the S06 oral history, the 2026 affidavit reporting. Attribution is handled at the passage, hostile witnesses are discounted (Williams, Uchitel, Haney with Steinberg's reply), and inference limits sit in the prose ('That is a reporter's synthesis', 'one friend, relayed and partly paraphrased'). But two context-fidelity errors hit load-bearing evidence: one unnamed friend becomes two (V-01, body and FAQ), and the Jordan splice drops the bridge that frames 'That bothers him' as regret over old mistakes (V-02). The standard asks for context-faithful, independent evidence, and these errors fall exactly at the independence and context of the type evidence. Smaller sourcing gaps (V-03 to V-05) are minor.

enneagram.passage: What tips against the One is where the pain lands: a One's torment is usually the inner critic, and Jordan describes torment over what people say.
enneagram.reason: The reasoning is honest and tested. The Eight gets its best evidence in plain view ('That scene is the Eight reading's best evidence'), the Five gets a fair reading of the costume and introvert material, Six and Seven are tested with sourced discriminators, the crisis sequence is correctly ruled non-discriminating, and confidence stays medium with named failures (SEAL chapter, aloofness, temper, slumps). The positive Three case is thinner than the counterevidence, though. It rests mostly on the 2010 achievement-as-license reading (a post-treatment account, as the article admits) and on one relayed friend's account, and this sentence overreads that account: in S17 Jordan's direct words are about wanting to undo 'the things that happened', which the article itself says is One territory. With V-02 repaired, the One and Three may sit closer than the prose now claims.
